beats: Hook: run a function on all 2^n inputs at once (line_qc_interfere_roller_cards: one stroke of a wide roller marks every card on the table): it sounds like unlimited parallelism. Then you measure and get one random answer (line_qc_interfere_lotto_drum). So where does a quantum speed-up actually come from? Same cast as QC07-01: the keeper and the rookie (cast drawing line_qc_revers_fresh_card).
H on every qubit gives all 2^n inputs (Q25-08 64:46-67:39): reuse line_two_lanterns (every fork doubles the paths).
Measure and you get one (67:41-68:21; clip 67:52-68:21); her 2024 caveat that superposition does not immediately give a speed-up (tape Q24-02 p32): line_qc_interfere_lotto_drum; reuse line_dice_hand.

H then H as two paths (68:45-70:52; clip 70:26-70:52, positive and negative interference): starting from |0>, both paths to 0 add up and the two paths to 1 cancel, so two Hadamards give back 0 for certain. The same thing with light: line_qc_interfere_two_paths (split a beam, bring it back together: one detector always clicks, the other stays dark; caption it as an optics analogue of H then H). Everyday version: pushes in step add, pushes against each other cancel (line_qc_interfere_swing_push); reuse line_qc_arrow_ripple_tank (QC04-02) for ripples crossing.
Why anything can cancel at all: amplitudes carry signs (QC04-02), probabilities never do; noise-cancelling headphones play the mirror-image wave (line_qc_interfere_noise_cancel).
The template: H, phase oracle, H, measure (71:17-72:12; Q25-09 18:27-19:04; tape Q25-09 s15); code draws the four stages.

The Hadamard transform H^n|x> = 2^(-n/2) sum_y (-1)^(x.y) |y> and the parity x.y (Q25-09 06:12-17:28: check in FACTS.md); "like a Fourier transform" (09:52-10:42): reuse line_qc_undo_two_prisms (QC05-01).

The design idea: arrange for the results you do not want to cancel out and the one you want to add up (clip Q24-13 28:17-28:42; her answer only, not the student question at 26:26-27:51): line_qc_interfere_tug_ropes.
Takeaway: superposition gives the room, interference does the work; next, the first algorithm built this way (QC07-05).

Cover (line_qc_cover_07_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): two playground swings: the keeper and the rookie push one together and it soars; they push the other from opposite sides and it does not move.
